title: [YouPass Collect] - High-speed internet connections: 2001–2002
prompt: The charts below give information about the high-speed continuous internet connection of households in five countries in 2001 and 2002. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart and table provide information about broadband internet subscriptions per 1000 residents in five nations, namely South Korea, the USA, Germany, Switzerland, and Britain, in 2001 and 2002, along with the corresponding percentage changes.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all five countries witnessed growth in high-speed internet connections over the given period. However, the USA and South Korea recorded significantly higher figures than the three European nations, while Britain experienced the most dramatic increase in percentage terms.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the leading countries, South Korea had the highest number of broadband connections in 2001, at 122 per 1000 people, followed by the USA with a slightly lower figure of 93. By 2002, the latter had surged to 251.1, representing a remarkable growth of 170%, thereby overtaking South Korea to become the top-ranked nation. Meanwhile, South Korea's figure rose more modestly to 134.4, equivalent to an increase of only 20%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the European countries, all three started at considerably lower levels in 2001, with figures ranging from just 3.3 to 3.6 connections per 1000 people. Britain showed the most impressive growth among these nations, with its numbers more than tripling to reach 10.89 in 2002, representing a substantial rise of 230%. Switzerland also experienced a notable increase, climbing to 7.92, which corresponded to a growth rate of 120%. Germany, despite recording the lowest growth rate of 80%, still saw its figure rise from 3.4 to 5.616 by the end of the period.
